The title omitted isotopy, although the Statement explicitly asserts beta ~ a stacking and equality only of classes in G_n. Changed only the title to match that claim. For n=1 the displayed linear contraction fixes both endpoints and stays in the disc. For n>=2 the crossing-wall interpolation preserves the strict order inequalities and signed vertical separation; inserting a standard configuration in a convex crossing-free chamber splits off the lowest crossing on the right. The published inversion definition uses the ordinal n, whereas this lemma acts on labels 1,...,n. Added explicit conjugation sigma_0=kappa sigma kappa^-1 with kappa(j)=j-1 and the order-preserving bijection of inversion sets. This is a nonfatal convention mismatch: all counts and inequalities in the local exchange calculation are preserved. Checked prefix crossing labels, the deletion identity t_c sigma=sigma s_j, and the triangular word for w_0. Read the full proof of Dehornoy et al. IX.1.11(ii), printed p.435: the imported induction uses exchange and finite rank-two orders, both established here, rather than assuming a Coxeter presentation.

For n>=2 the empty family has every sigma_1^k as a common divisor, so a greatest common divisor would have length at least k for all k. This disproves the original universal finite-family clause. Restored the nonempty hypothesis of the cited gcd theorem and bounded candidates by the length of one input member. The normal-form algorithm still uses only the nonempty pair {Delta,[u]}; reversing decides its tests, power extraction drops length by N>=1, and the cited greedy factorisation theorem guarantees proper factors and Delta-free successive tails.

The comparison remark overstates coverage: the theorem assumes n>2 and the comparison proposition assumes n=2. Restricted that remark to n>=2, leaving the theorem unchanged. Its proof is valid: Delta^(2r)=cb clears the denominator of a central x=ab^-1 to ac; the positive-center lemma gives an even Delta power, and the embedding and positive length make Delta^2 nonidentity. Torsion freeness then makes the surjective integer-power map injective. Neither n=0 nor n=1 is a hypothesis of the theorem.

The remark contradicted its own correct numbers: the positive word for Delta has three letters and (sigma_1 sigma_2)^3 has six, so their exponent sums are 3 and 6, not the same. Removed that false equality. The verification remains valid: the braid relation makes the two length-three factors Delta, applying the index reversal twice proves centrality of Delta^2, and the distinct transposition images plus monoid embedding show Delta is not central. The center theorem at n=3 supplies the infinite cyclic description.
